title: Complexity and Chaos
lead: Some systems that obey the simple laws of physics are complex enough to organize themselves, adapt and evolve. This section describes complexity, the emerging field that studies such systems, and chaos, the study of systems whose outcomes depend extremely sensitively on how they start, and how order can arise within them.
objectives: Discuss chaotic behavior of different systems.
summary_html:
• Complexity is an emerging field, rooted primarily in physics, that considers complex adaptive systems and their evolution, including self-organization.
  • Complexity has applications in physics and many other disciplines, such as biological evolution.
  • Chaos is a field that studies systems whose properties depend extremely sensitively on some variables and whose evolution is impossible to predict.
  • Chaotic systems may be simple or complex.
  • Studies of chaos have led to methods for understanding and predicting certain chaotic behaviors.

exercises.prompt: Must a complex system be adaptive to be of interest in the field of complexity? Give an example to support your answer.

answer.solution: No. Complexity is devoted to the study of complex systems in general; their ability to adapt and evolve is of particular interest, but it is not a requirement. The book names complex systems in traditional physics that complexity may shed light on without their adapting as living things do: crystal growth, in which self-organization emerges spontaneously, alloys, and iron atoms organizing into magnetic domains as they cool. A growing crystal organizes itself, yet it does not adapt to its surroundings or evolve the way a biological or an economic system does.

exercises.prompt: State a necessary condition for a system to be chaotic.

answer.solution: Its outcome must be extremely sensitive to its initial conditions: two starts that differ by a tiny amount must lead, in time, to outcomes that differ greatly, so that its long-term behavior cannot be predicted with precision. Two double pendulums released at angles that differ by a thousandth of a degree swing together at first and then move quite differently, as Pluto's orbit may change tremendously because of small interactions with the other planets.
